analysis:
The PR is CI-only. It adds two actionlint runner labels (.github/actionlint.yaml:13-14) and a `route` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (head ~22-35). The route job calls a reusable workflow, ./.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml, with `permissions: {}`. Six jobs now take `runs-on` from `fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[...]`, so they can land on Darkbloom Sandboxes or on the Blacksmith fallback. Timeouts are added, and provider-test-gate moves to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04. No provider, coordinator, attestation, key, cache or fan-helper code changes, so I found no change to A-001, A-003, A-010, A-015/16/17, TB-002/009/011 or T-041.

One question is not resolved by the supplied evidence. These routed jobs run on `pull_request` and execute PR-controlled code: submodule checkout and builds, `swift test`, and `npm ci`. If darkbloom-route.yml can send fork or untrusted PRs to a persistent self-hosted Darkbloom Sandbox, that is a runner-compromise and secret-exposure surface. The sandboxes' ephemerality, isolation, secret exposure and fork gating are not shown. The routing workflow, its scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, and the label-fallback logic are outside the supplied diff. I record this as an unverified contract rather than a finding. The routes output is also consumed through `fromJSON` as a runner label, so whether a malformed or attacker-influenced lane string can select an unintended runner depends on the route workflow's validation. The next pass should review darkbloom-route.yml, including its fork and untrusted-PR handling, the runner trust level, the secrets available to those jobs, and whether `routes` is built from trusted constants only. The ci.yml patch excerpt is truncated, but the base and head texts show the remaining changes are consistent with the same routing pattern.
